content: We develop the theory, algorithms, and hardware-tested systems that enable autonomous robots to act intelligently — even under uncertainty, resource constraints, and incomplete information. Our techniques bridge optimal control, reinforcement learning, machine learning, and mathematical optimization.
Our work spans the full spectrum — from fundamental mathematical theory to robots operating in the real world.

We combine data-driven methods with Hamilton–Jacobi (HJ) reachability and control barrier functions (CBFs) to study provable safety for autonomous robots. Our work addresses the computational cost of high-dimensional systems and the limitations of safety methods that require accurate dynamic models.

items: Safety guarantees for learned controllers.
We study conditions under which neural networks and reinforcement learning methods satisfy the safety guarantees of HJ reachability and CBFs.
Connections between CBFs and reachability.
We study the relationship between these frameworks to develop principled methods for constructing control barrier functions.
Least-conservative safety filters.
We seek safety conditions that preserve the widest possible set of control actions while maintaining formal safety guarantees.
Safe navigation under uncertainty.
We develop and test safe autonomy methods for incomplete sensing, unknown environments, and semantic constraints on physical robots.
Conditions for learned safety guarantees.
We establish theoretical conditions under which learned safety methods provide provable guarantees.

We develop real-time controllers that update their decisions as new sensor information becomes available. Our research addresses computational limits, disturbances, and model uncertainty through efficient optimal control solvers, robust model predictive control, and receding horizon planning. Faster computation supports longer planning horizons within a fixed time budget.

items: Efficient optimal control solvers.
We use Hopf–Lax theory to develop numerical methods for computing optimal control solutions in real time.
Convexification of nonlinear control problems.
We investigate reformulations of nonlinear optimal control problems as convex problems to improve computational tractability.
Optimal control formulations of robust control.
We study conditions under which robust control problems can be recast as optimal control problems and solved using efficient numerical methods.
Robust sampling-based control.
We develop Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) methods that evaluate candidate trajectories in parallel on GPUs and compute control actions under disturbances.
Real-time receding horizon planning.
We develop controllers that repeatedly solve a finite-horizon planning problem and update the plan as the environment or available information changes.
